conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Thank you. Do you have a family doctor, and if so, what is their name?

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Thank you. Do you currently have a psychiatrist, and if so, what is their name?

conversation.message: Yes, I do — Dr. Laura Bennett.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Thank you. What are the main problems or concerns bringing you in today?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: It’s… mostly my son’s death. The grief has been overwhelming, and I’m so sad all the time. I just can’t seem to concentrate properly either, everything feels kind of foggy.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: I’m very sorry for your loss, David. What would you most like to accomplish through counseling or treatment?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: I want to cope with the loss better… and get back to functioning properly, really. Also to honour his memory, if that makes sense.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Thank you for sharing that. Have you ever been assessed by a mental-health professional before, and if so, what were the details?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes… I was followed by Dr. Laura Bennett, the psychiatrist, during two depressive episodes back in 1998 and 2003.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Thank you. Were you given any psychiatric diagnoses during those assessments?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Sorry, when you say diagnoses… do you mean the actual label they put on it, or just what was going on at the time? I’m a bit tangled up.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: I mean the formal mental-health labels or conditions you were told you had, if any. What were they?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Depression. I had two prior episodes, in my 30s.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Thank you. Were you ever admitted to a psychiatric hospital, and if so, what happened?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: No, I wasn’t admitted to hospital.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Have you ever intentionally harmed yourself or had thoughts of harming yourself, and if so, could you tell me when and what happened?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: No, I’ve never intentionally harmed myself. Well… I do get thoughts that I’d be better off dead sometimes, but I don’t have any plan or intent to act on it. It’s more just… wishing I wasn’t here, especially with everything that’s happened.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Thank you for telling me, David. Because you’re having thoughts of being better off dead, please contact 988 in Canada or your local emergency number if you feel at risk or these thoughts become harder to control; if you’re in immediate danger, call 911 or go to an emergency department. Do you feel safe right now, and do you have any current intention or plan to harm yourself?
